item.description: Deaths from rectal cancer are rising rapidly among younger adults, an alarming trend that is confounding scientists trying to understand why millennials are so hard-hit.

media:content.media:text: Closeup view of physician colonoscopy to patient in a clinic.
media:content.media:description: The American Cancer Society recommends that colorectal cancer screening begin at age 45 for people at average risk of the disease. If the results are normal, a follow-up colonoscopy can be done in 10 years.

item.description: President Trump announced that he was pulling the nomination of Dr. Casey Means for surgeon general, and announced that she would be replaced with Dr. Nicole Saphier, who is listed on Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center's website as a radiologist and director of breast imaging at its facility in Monmouth County, New Jersey.
